DurationMs.description:
A LENGTH of time in milliseconds. Not a position.

This docstring read "Duration or audio position" until 2026-08-15, and
the `or` was the defect: one type standing for two facts means nothing
can notice a length passed where an offset belongs. `MediaWindow` stored
its two file offsets in it for exactly that reason.

A POSITION measured from the start of a recording is
`batchalign::time::FileMs`; one measured from the start of an alignment
window is `batchalign::time::WindowMs`. Use those for offsets, and this
only for genuine durations (`max_group_ms`, `tight_buffer_ms`).

Still carried by the `worker_v2` IPC types, whose `start_ms` / `end_ms`
fields ARE positions and are not yet converted. Two DIFFERENT decisions
hide behind that, and only one waits on anyone else: the wire type here
mirrors the Python side, but the hop after it
(`batchalign::chat_ops::nlp::types::FaIndexedTiming`) is entirely ours,
is not Python-facing, and serializes identically to a `WindowMs`. Typing
that one needs no coordination. See `batchalign::time` for what else
blocks retiring the duplicate `Ms`, and for which direction a merge
would have to go.

RequestedRevisionV2.description:
What the plan asked a worker to load.

[`Self::Unpinned`] is a real state, not a placeholder: a user may name an
arbitrary hub model this build has no pin for, and if plan-time resolution
cannot reach the hub the honest answer is "load the default and tell me
what you got". It has its own admission rule (the worker MUST report a
commit) and it can never build a cache key.

SpeakerAttributionV2.description:
Who a provider attributed one monologue to.

Two states, because there are two facts, and the wire used to have a
spelling for only one of them. `speaker` was a bare string, so an engine
that separates no speakers at all (Aliyun, FunASR, Whisper, Qwen) had to
write SOMETHING, and what it wrote was `"0"`: a label indistinguishable
from a provider's real first speaker. Downstream that became
`SpeakerIndex(0)` and a `PAR0` tier, so "nobody was diarized" and "the
provider said speaker zero" produced identical CHAT.

`Undiarized` is now a state of its own, and an ABSENT label where
separation WAS requested is a refusal rather than a track number.

oneOf.description: The provider named a speaker; this is its own label for them.

label.description: The provider's label, exactly as it spelled it.

oneOf.description:
The provider separates no speakers and named none. This is a claim
about the ENGINE, not a guess about the recording.

SpeakerEmbeddingOutcomeV2.description:
What the embedding model had to say about one requested span.

Two variants, because "we could not measure this" and "we measured this"
are different facts and only one of them is a vector. Below its own minimum
input length the pinned model does not raise: it returns a correctly shaped
float array whose every component is NaN, which no type can distinguish
from a real embedding and which compares false against every threshold. A
caller handed that would report an utterance as UNMATCHED when the honest
answer is UNMEASURABLE. The worker refuses instead, and says how short.

oneOf.description: The model measured this span.

vector.description: Fixed-width acoustic vector, whose width the envelope declares.

oneOf.description: The span is shorter than the model's own minimum input length.

frame_count.description:
How many frames the span held. The minimum it fell short of is on
the envelope, which owns that fact once for the whole response.

SpeakerEmbeddingResultV2.description:
Speaker embeddings for every requested span, plus the model's own bounds.

`dimension` and `minimum_frames` are REPORTED by the worker rather than
assumed by the reader. They are properties of the loaded model file, so a
constant on this side would be a second place the truth lives and would go
on agreeing with a model that had moved.

dimension.description: Width of every `Embedded` vector in this response.

minimum_frames.description: Shortest span the model will measure, in prepared-audio frames.

spans.description: One outcome per requested span, in the order requested.

SpeakerEmbeddingSpanIdV2.description:
Caller-chosen name for one span of a speaker-embedding request.

Echoed verbatim in the response so the control plane pairs an outcome
with the span it asked about BY NAME. Pairing two sequences by position
is the shape that silently attributes one speaker's acoustic evidence
to another utterance, and no arity check catches a reordering.

SpeakerEmbeddingSpanResultV2.description: One requested span's outcome, echoing the id it was requested under.

outcome.description: What the model had to say about it.

span_id.description: The requested span's name, echoed verbatim.

UdRelationRepairKindV2.description: Why one Universal Dependencies relation a worker received from Stanza is not the relation it applied. Closed: a worker cannot report a repair not named here.

UdRelationRepairV2.description:
One relation rewrite a worker made inside an analysis it returned.

Carries what it takes to attribute the rewrite as well as count it: the
word it was made on, and both relations. The worker is the only witness,
because the relation Stanza produced does not survive into the analysis it
sends: by the time the server sees the item, the repaired relation is the
only one there.

to_relation.description:
The relation applied in its place, which the worker admits is a UD
relation before it builds this value.

word.description:
Surface form of the word whose relation was rewritten, so a reader can
find it in the transcript.

UtsegBoundaryModelEvidenceV2.description:
Provenance-bearing evidence emitted by one boundary-model invocation.

The wrapper prevents a per-word evidence vector from traveling without the
model identity needed to interpret or reproduce it.

model_id.description: HuggingFace model identifier the control plane pinned.

model_revision.description:
The exact revision the worker loaded, and never anything else.

Required, and a [`HubCommitV2`] rather than a string: the boundary model
is resolved from a pinned snapshot whose commit is read off the
directory on disk, so a worker that cannot say which revision it loaded
refuses instead of reporting one. It was `Option<String>` while the
model loaded by NAME and the revision was scraped from
`config._commit_hash`, which could simply be absent; nothing downstream
could distinguish "no revision" from "a revision nobody recorded".

WhisperChunkResultV2.description: One ASR result built from raw Whisper chunks.

model.description:
The models that produced this result, as the runtime observed them.

Required, and deliberately not defaulted: a transcript whose models are
unknown cannot be stamped honestly or cached safely, and an optional
field would let every producer forget to fill it while still
compiling. The only route to a value is a loader that actually loaded
something, so "which models produced this text" is answered by
construction rather than by a downstream lookup that can miss.
